intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the MPZ gene (159440) on chromosome 1q23.3.

checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature not stated in the abstract; accepted as restating gene identity.

paragraphs.text: Congenital hypomyelination is a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy. It starts in early infancy and causes distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severely slowed nerve conduction velocities (Mandich et al., 1999). Onset may be prenatal, neonatal, or early infantile. Most reported patients die within the first years of life, and histopathology shows absent or thin myelin sheaths (Smit et al., 2008).

paragraphs.text: Kochanski et al. (2004) described the clinical and morphologic features of a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy (CHN). They described CHN as a severe neuropathy with onset in early infancy. In CHN, sural nerve biopsy showed nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons, with basal lamina onion bulbs and no myelin breakdown products.

paragraphs.text: Smit et al. (2008) reported a long-term follow-up study of a family with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy. Affected members were found in 2 generations. The authors noted that CHN is a rare condition with prenatal, neonatal, or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis, and areflexia, and that most reported patients die within the first years of life.

paragraphs.text: Warner et al. (1996) identified 5 novel mutations in the MPZ gene in patients with CMT1B, DSS, or congenital hypomyelination. MPZ encodes P0, the major structural protein of peripheral nerve myelin. The authors suggested that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities. Instead, they may form a spectrum of related 'myelinopathies' caused by an underlying defect in myelination.
